questions.text: What variable holds the default error message from @error directives?
questions.explanation: Inside an @error('field') ... @enderror block, Blade provides $message, the first error message for that field. $errors is the bag holding all validation errors, available in every view.

questions.text: What does the following code allow?
options: It prevents name and email from being changed after saving.
It makes name and email required fields in the database
It allows name and email to be assigned when saving model data.
It makes name and email automatically unique.
questions.explanation: $fillable whitelists the attributes that can be mass-assigned, e.g. through Model::create($request->all()). It says nothing about required, unique or read-only columns.

questions.text: Which command creates a migration for a products table?
questions.explanation: php artisan make:migration create_products_table creates a timestamped migration file in database/migrations. The create_..._table name also tells Laravel to pre-fill a Schema::create('products', ...) stub.

questions.text: Which modifier allows a column to store NULL or optional value?
What is created by this statement?
questions.warning: The quiz writes timestamp() but means timestamps() (plural). The singular timestamp('name') creates one TIMESTAMP column and needs a column name.
questions.explanation: $table->timestamps(); adds the nullable created_at and updated_at columns that Eloquent fills in automatically.

questions.text: You are tasked with creating a form in Laravel that submits customer suggestions to a controller, processes the input, validates it, and then displays the suggestions on another page. Analyze the snippet and choose from the table to fill in the blanks with the correct code snippets in the provided sections: Route, Controller, View (Form), and View (Display).
questions.explanation:
1. submit: the route points at the controller method, which is named submit.
  2. validate: $request->validate([...]) checks the input and redirects back with errors if it fails.
  3. view: view('suggestions.display', [...]) renders the display page with the data.
  4. suggestion.submit: route() takes the route's name, set by ->name('suggestion.submit').
  5. csrf: @csrf adds the hidden token every POST form needs.
  6. err: the loop variable is $err (as $err), so each message is {{ $err }}.
  7. suggest: the controller passed the suggestion under the key 'suggest', so the view sees $suggest, not $suggestion.

questions.text: Which character is used to separate multiple validation rules for a single field?
questions.explanation: Rules in a string are separated by a pipe: 'email' => 'required|email|max:255'. (You can also pass them as an array, ['required', 'email'], but the separator character is |.)

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the down() method in a migration?
options: To reverse the changes made by up()
To connect MYSQL to Laravel project
questions.explanation: down() undoes whatever up() did, and it runs on rollback. Dropping the table is only what it does when up() created one. If up() added a column, down() removes that column instead.

questions.text: Which statement creates a VARCHAR-style column?
questions.explanation: string() creates a VARCHAR column (255 by default). char() is fixed-length CHAR, text() is a TEXT column, and there's no varchar() method.

questions.text: How do you validate a request inside a controller?
questions.explanation: $request->validate([...]) runs the rules and, if any fail, redirects back with $errors and the old input. The other three aren't Laravel methods.

questions.text: What validation rule ensures the field password is present and not empty?
questions.explanation: required fails if the field is missing, null or an empty string. The real rule for matching a confirmation field is confirmed (not confirm), and notnull doesn't exist.

questions.text: What will be the display output if $temperature is 15?
questions.context:
@if ($temperature < 0)
    <h2 class="temperature-status">It's freezing cold!</h2>
@elseif ($temperature > 0 && $temperature < 15)
    <h2 class="temperature-status">It's quite chilly.</h2>
@elseif ($temperature > 15 && $temperature < 25)
    <h2 class="temperature-status">The weather is pleasant.</h2>
@else
    <h2 class="temperature-status">It's hot outside!</h2>
@endif
questions.explanation: All the comparisons are strict. 15 isn't < 15 (so not chilly) and isn't > 15 (so not pleasant). No branch matches, so it falls through to @else: "It's hot outside!"

questions.text: Which method contains the database changes that should be applied when a migration runs?
questions.explanation: php artisan migrate runs each migration's up() method; down() reverses it on rollback.

questions.text: Which modifier assigns a value automatically when no value is supplied?
Which command rolls back all migrations?
questions.explanation: migrate:reset rolls back every migration. migrate:rollback only undoes the last batch (or --step=N), and migrate:drop / migrate:clear don't exist.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a directive used in Laravel Blade for switch?
questions.warning: Outside Source says @endswitch, but all four options are real Blade switch directives, so there's no right answer here.
questions.explanation: FLAGGED AS A BROKEN QUESTION. A Blade switch is written @switch ... @case ... @break ... @default ... @endswitch, so every listed option is a valid directive. @endswitch closes every switch block. The question probably meant to include a fake directive like @enddefault, as in Quiz 1. Worth reporting to the instructor.

questions.text: Which input satisfies the following rule?
questions.explanation: digits_between:5,8 requires a numeric value with 5 to 8 digits. 113466 has 6. 178656789 and 567887667 have 9, and 5855 has only 4.

questions.text: What variable holds the error messages from all of the validation errors in a Laravel Blade template?
questions.explanation: $errors is a MessageBag shared with every view; use $errors->all() or $errors->any(). $message only exists inside an @error block and holds one field's message.

questions.text: Laravel uses CSRF tokens in the form of hidden fields for GET _token requests to prevent unauthorized access and to secure each user submission.
questions.warning: Outside Source says True. It's keyed False here because Laravel doesn't check CSRF tokens on GET requests, only on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
questions.explanation: Laravel does put the CSRF token in a hidden _token field (via @csrf), but its CSRF middleware skips read-only requests (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) and verifies the token only on state-changing ones like POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. The "GET" makes the statement false as written. If the quiz meant "POST", it would be true.
